purpose: Ground truth for the seven-category process-activity vocabulary on the client's rebar hall. Gates C.0 in docs/prd/slice-chronometraz.md (gpu-exchange).

pass_bar.measured_on: manually annotated material held out of the training set

camera.name: hala prawe skrzydlo
camera.framing: whole-hall 4K fisheye, NOT station-framed - the client declined to reframe (assumption A2, falsified 2026-08-28)
camera.pose_rationale: 640x640 resolves nobody under 360 native px and reports recall_risk=high; 1280x736 halves the floor to 180 px and flips the verdict to normal. Activity accuracy is capped by detection recall, so annotating 640 footage would measure the wrong thing.

activities.note: Not an activity. The annotator's and the classifier's honest 'cannot tell'. Never counted as work or downtime.

delivery_vocabulary.why: The three-category scope the client accepted from the #117 feasibility report: spawanie, ukladanie_pretow, and everything else as one collective line. Every figure in that report was produced on seven categories, so the vocabulary actually being delivered had never been scored (#121).
delivery_vocabulary.excludes: nierozpoznane is deliberately NOT a member and keeps its own row. The manifest defines it as never work and never downtime, and the client report says the same; folding the honest cannot-tell into a collective work bucket would convert 3.4% of unknown time into measured time.
delivery_vocabulary.integrity: The categories were fixed by the client acceptance of the #117 scope, which predates this scoring - the mapping is not chosen from arm results. But seven-category arm results WERE already known when this block was written, so like the 3-fold split it is not a blind pre-registration, and it is recorded that way rather than implied to be one.
delivery_vocabulary.never_mix: A three-category figure is not comparable with a seven-category one and the two must never appear in the same table. evaluate_arms.py enforces the separation in the renderer; a reader cannot undo a merge by reading harder.

clips.provenance: NOT a platform task, unlike W1/W2. Cut by hand from the appliance's rolling buffer on cctv-vps-camera - 20 consecutive one-minute chunks concatenated with stream copy, so the frames are the recorder's own and were never re-encoded. Container metadata is honest: r_frame_rate=20/1, 23985 frames over 1200.04 s, so W1's 120/1 trap does not recur here.
clips.source_retained: The full three-hour buffer this was cut from (18:21-21:21 local, 180 chunks, 6.8 GB) is preserved at ~/preserve-2026-09-01-zmiana2 on cctv-vps-camera, outside the rotating buffer. Further windows can be cut from it without re-capturing. That directory is NOT backed up and lives on one machine.
clips.note: Recovered because the C.0 report named the missing second-half-of-shift material as the open question. The original DROPPED decision and its cost stand as history: W1 and W2 are still both pre-break, so any figure computed over those two alone still carries that bias, and two of the three windows still do.

split.declared_before_any_model_run_note: TRUE for the original 2-fold protocol, declared 2026-09-01 before a single arm ran, and FALSE for this one. Three arms had already been measured when the third window was added. The flag is set honestly rather than carried over, because a split whose provenance is asserted but not true is worse than no split at all - it launders a retrofit as a discipline. Read every 3-fold figure with that attached.
split.reporting: Per-activity accuracy is computed on the UNION of the three folds' held-out predictions - every labelled sample is predicted exactly once, by a model that never saw it. One confusion matrix per arm over that union, plus the per-fold matrices so a fold-specific collapse is visible.
split.rule: Within a fold, no arm is tuned, prompted, thresholded or trained on that fold's held-out window. An arm that cannot honour fold isolation (e.g. a hand-tuned threshold fitted on both) is reported as such and its figure is marked in-sample.

amended_2.why: W3 exists and is annotated, and it fixes the specific defect the 2-fold split could not work around: brak_na_stanowisku and nierozpoznane were used almost disjointly by the two windows (66/0 and 2/58), so under 2-fold each model was asked for a class it had never seen and both scored a meaningless 0.0%. W3 contributes 24 and 4, so every fold now trains on at least some of both. sciaganie_elementu also rises from 52 held-out samples to 110, and the fixture stops being entirely pre-break.
amended_2.integrity_warning: UNLIKE the first amendment, this one is made AFTER arm results are known on the old split. That is a real difference and it is recorded rather than glossed: a figure produced under 3-fold is NOT comparable to the arm figures already published under 2-fold, and the two must never be quoted in the same table. Anything measured from here is a fresh measurement of a re-scoped fixture, not an improvement on the old number.
amended_2.does_not_fix: postoj. W3 adds 4 samples - eight seconds in twenty minutes - for 62 across all three windows. The activity is rare at this station rather than under-sampled, so no amount of comparable footage rescues it. nierozpoznane is also still thin in one direction: the fold holding out W2 trains on only 4 examples of it.

amended.was: single split, W1 train / W2 held out
amended.why: The single split cannot measure the per-activity bar, which is the bar. Class support on W2 alone: brak_na_stanowisku n=2 (one error moves the score 50 pp - unmeasurable), postoj n=16 (6.2 pp per error), and nierozpoznane n=0 on W1 so a trained arm would have no examples of it at all. Under 2-fold every class clears 52 held-out samples: spawanie 497, ukladanie_pretow 359, inna_czynnosc 107, brak_na_stanowisku 68, nierozpoznane 58, postoj 58, sciaganie_elementu 52.
amended.integrity: Amended on ANNOTATION statistics only, before any spike arm ran - no model result informed it. That distinction is the whole point of declaring a split early, so it is recorded rather than quietly rewritten.

split.caveat: Three windows, one station, two operators, two of the three pre-break. Cross-validation bounds overfitting to one window; it does not establish transfer to another station. Two confounds are now entangled and this fixture cannot separate them: W3 differs from W1/W2 in BOTH shift and operator, so a drop on W3 could be either and calling it 'the afternoon is harder' would be unsupported. Aggregate figures still lean pre-break, two windows to one. With three folds the variance on a small class stays wide; treat anything under ~100 held-out samples as indicative, not settled.

station_roi.note: The welding bench. C.0 is measured INSIDE this ROI, cropped from the native frame - not from the 1280x736 downscale, which would discard the 3x that makes station framing work. This is the software crop that discharges assumption A2 (client refused a physical reframe; nothing forbids cropping pixels we already receive).

verification.method: keyframe inspection + 1 fps saturated-pixel scan (Y>235) inside station_roi
verification.arc_metric_caveat: Clip-relative, not a portable constant - the two windows differ ~3x at the median, so ambient light drift alone moves a fixed cut-off. Detects ARC, not welding WORK: it cannot separate ukladanie_pretow from postoj. Use as a weak pre-label for spawanie and as the cost floor any GPU model must beat, never as ground truth.
verification.vocabulary_gap_reproducible: The operator mid-arc, sparks visible, is labelled `standing` by the shipped four-pose classifier, and `standing` maps to `Praca` in this camera's activity_label_map. Welding and standing idle are the same label today.
verification.frame_rate_trap: W1 reports r_frame_rate=120/1 in container metadata; the true rate is ~20 fps (23959 frames / 1198.03 s). W2 reports 20/1 correctly. Annotation tooling must index by pts_time, never by frame number, or every W1 timestamp is wrong.

retention_note: RESOLVED, and the near-miss is the lesson. r2_key_original pointed into the appliance-uploads prefix, which the C-5 retention reaper deletes on task completion (gpu-exchange, feat(retention) 3e2d8e8, committed 2026-08-28 09:51 CEST, deployed to production the same day 17:34 CEST). Both originals WERE reaped - verified 2026-09-01: the appliance-uploads keys are gone and both tasks read inputUploadIds: []. The r2_key_preserved copies were made by hand at 11:04 CEST, ~6.5 h before the reaper went live, and survive because they sit outside the prefix findReapableTaskInputs can select. There is no second copy and the appliance buffer is only 3 h deep, so this material is IRREPLACEABLE. Nothing in the repo automates the preserve step - it remains a manual action, and the platform has no retention-hold flag.
